2610.05782.title: Agentic-ZTA: A Multi-Agent Architecture for Autonomous Zero Trust Enforcement
2610.05782.paper_summary: Agentic AI is emerging as a promising paradigm for automating complex cybersecurity decisions, yet its use in enforcing zero trust introduces significant challenges in safety, reliability, and policy compliance. This paper presents Agentic AI based zero trust architecture (Agentic-ZTA) that operationalizes the NIST SP 800-207 ZTA architecture control loop through coordinated multi- agent decision pipeline. In the proposed framework, policy knowledge is embedded into a retrieval-augmented generation pipeline and retrieved at inference time as top-k relevant policies. Access requests are intercepted by the Policy Enforcement Point (PEP), enriched with contextual metadata. The request context is routed to a policy engine agent which invokes domain-specialized core agents first followed by supporting agents, if further evaluation needed. AI agents reason over access context, policy constraints and determine trust. The retrieved policies are embedded into agent prompt during inference time and agentic trust scores are aggregated and evaluated by a trust-algorithm, producing the final access decision for enforcement under continuous verification. We implement Agentic-ZTA in a testbed and evaluate it on representative access-control use cases scenarios. Our Agentic-ZTA framework achieves 95.0% accuracy, 93.9% precision, and 96.3% recall, and demonstrate the feasibility of enforcing zero trust using AI agents.
2610.05782.paper_summary_zh: 代理人工智慧正在成為自動化複雜網路安全決策的一個有前景的範式，但其在執行零信任時引入了安全性、可靠性和政策遵從性方面的重大挑戰。本文提出了一種基於代理人工智慧的零信任架構（Agentic-ZTA），通過協調的多代理決策管道來操作化NIST SP 800-207 ZTA架構控制迴路。在所提出的框架中，政策知識被嵌入到檢索增強生成管道中，並在推理時作為前k個相關政策進行檢索。訪問請求被政策執行點（PEP）攔截，並豐富了上下文元數據。請求上下文被路由到政策引擎代理，該代理首先調用領域專業的核心代理，然後在需要進一步評估的情況下調用支持代理。人工智慧代理根據訪問上下文、政策約束進行推理並確定信任。檢索到的政策在推理時嵌入到代理提示中，代理信任分數由信任算法進行聚合和評估，生成最終的訪問決策以便在持續驗證下執行。我們在測試平台上實現了Agentic-ZTA，並在代表性的訪問控制用例場景中對其進行評估。我們的Agentic-ZTA框架達到了95.0%的準確率、93.9%的精確率和96.3%的召回率，並展示了使用人工智慧代理執行零信任的可行性。
